title: The hierarchy of accuracy: why bars beat pies

videos.script: Here is Horta's revenue last year, split into six product categories. As a pie. {{pie}} Which category is largest? Vegetables or Fruit? Take a moment. {{guess}} Most people hesitate here. The two slices differ by about one percentage point, and the eye is not good at angles. {{close}} Now the same six numbers as bars, sorted from largest to smallest. {{bars}} Vegetables is first. Fruit is second. The question has gone away. {{answer}} This is not a matter of taste. In 1984 two statisticians at Bell Labs, William Cleveland and Robert McGill, measured it. They showed people pairs of marks and asked them to judge the ratio. {{experiment}} Position on a shared scale came out most accurate. Length next. Angle and area much worse. {{ranking}} This lesson gives you that ranking, explains why area is read short, and shows the one job a pie still does well. {{plan}}
